To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GAD67 mRNA is the predominant GAD mRNA in the spinal cord during embryonic and early postnatal life, that EP10 mRNA is the predominant variant in the embryonic spinal cord, and that GAD65 mRNA is the predominant isoform in the adult spinal cord.

the developmental expression of GAD family genes parallels that of GABAergic neurons and that the developmental kinetics of GAD-related mRNA expression are consistent with the operation of a feedback loop that is sensitive to the level of GABA.
the developmental kinetics of GAD mRNAs in the spinal cord are consistent with the hypothesis that GABAergic neurons are born in the ventral cord, then migrate dorsally and differentiate.

GABAergic neurons are generated in the spinal cord in a highly coordinated fashion that is consistent with a model in which the expression of GABAA and GABA receptors is regulated by the expression of GDA mRNAs, the synthesis of GABA, and the activation of GABAA receptors.

The main takeaway from our work is that
GAD-related mRNAS are present early and are regulated by a complex feedback loop, and that GABA is present at a time when the neurons are being formed.
the GABAergic system is fully operational in the embryo and that GAD67 expression in the ventricular zone is associated with the generation of neurons.

the developmental kinetics of GAD-related genes and their products parallel neurogenesis in a region-specific manner, and that these mRNAs may be useful markers of neuronal development in the spinal cord.
